Semi-retired harbour pilot with a history of hypertension and chronic kidney disease presents for urological follow-up following a prior transperineal prostate biopsy. He resides in a ground-floor apartment with his partner and maintains close contact with his sister, who serves as his primary next-of-kin. The patient reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms consistent with an IPSS of 18, alongside a 17 pack-year smoking history and weekly alcohol consumption of approximately 27 units. Mobility is currently restricted to chair-based exercises due to osteoarthritis, and he recently attended routine outpatient visits for thyroid screening, knee follow-up, and a chest radiograph. He notes that he is hard of hearing and consistently requests written summaries of clinical discussions to ensure accurate comprehension.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate is non-palpable with no discrete nodules or asymmetry, correlating with a clinical stage of cT1c. General inspection reveals a well-nourished individual with stable vital signs and no signs of peripheral oedema or lymphadenopathy.
